column1: # The graded admission suite. The five-prompt screen separates the 4B from the
# 9B no further, so a candidate that crosses a throughput threshold needs a
# suite that resolves the quality it trades away. Every row is graded by a
# program rather than by reading, because forty-five prompts read by hand
# reward the reader's memory of the previous candidate.
#   numeric        expectation is the answer; the last number in the reply must
#                  equal it within a relative tolerance of 1e-6
#   contains_all   expectation is a |-separated list; every entry must appear
#   contains_any   expectation is a |-separated list; one entry suffices
#   json_keys      the reply must parse as JSON and hold every |-separated key
#   regex          expectation is a Python regular expression, searched
#   nonempty       the reply must hold a non-whitespace answer, which is what a
#                  reasoning-termination failure withholds; a reply cut at the
#                  token budget refuses it, because the row asks whether the
#                  model stopped and a truncated reply was stopped
#   tool_call      the emitted tool_calls must match `name:key=value|key=value`,
#                  with `;` between calls where a row expects more than one
#   no_tool_call   the reply must carry no tool call and must hold one of the
#                  |-separated substrings, which is the row a tool set is
#                  offered on and should not be reached for
# The attachment column names what the request carries besides the prompt. `-`
# is the prompt alone. `image:NAME` sends remote/quality-images/NAME.png or .jpg;
# several names separated by `|` send several images in order. `tools:SET`
# The `vision` fixtures are drawn by remote/generate-quality-images.py and each
# row grades against a fact that file declares, so the answer is known by
# construction rather than by a reader's impression. The `photo` fixture is a
# photograph, pinned by remote/download-quality-photo.sh, and its rows grade
# against facts read off that exact file. The two categories stay apart because
# they test different things: drawn art gives the projector hard edges and a
# handful of exact RGB values, where a camera image gives it sensor noise, depth
# of field, resampling, and JPEG artefacts. A model that reads charts and fails
# on a photograph is a failure one merged category would average away.
# A tool row executes nothing. The appliance runs without --tools, so the server
# holds no tool server and runs no command; the request body's `tools` field
# asks the model to emit a `tool_calls` object and the grader reads that object.
# Tool selection is measured with the read-only boundary intact rather than
# The five original prompts are retained as the `screen` category so a
# candidate's suite result stays comparable to every figure already recorded.
